jordan_cust: Hey folks — hitting a pretty bad production issue with streaming. Connections drop ~every 30s and when our client reconnects the python iterator yields partial JSON fragments and sometimes replays tokens. Billing spike noticed. SDK v0.9.1. Request id: req_0abc1234. Any quick ideas?

amy_support: Sorry about that, Jordan — we'll triage. Can you paste a minimal repro + the raw logs around the reconnect? Also are you rotating tokens mid-stream?

jordan_cust: Not intentional, but we do have short-lived tokens (5m) with auto-rotate. Repro steps (super minimal):
```py
async for chunk in client.stream("/v1/stream", input=prompt):
    process(chunk)
# simulate network blip (tcp kill) then reconnect
```
Logs show reconnect then iterator emits `{"partial": "...}` fragments and occasionally repeats a fragment we already processed. Server-side shows handshake accepted then a 502 for the next handshake.

bob_oncall: tagging in — looking at the server logs for req_0abc1234 now. Two quick thoughts: 1) token rotation during an active resume handshake can cause resume offset drift if the resume token map isn't atomically swapped; 2) heartbeat timestamps drifting between client and edge can cause the client to think connection is stale and reconnect quickly (thundering).

bob_oncall: snippet from edge logs (redacted):
```
[2026-02-15T14:02:13Z] req_0abc1234 handshake ok; resume_token=rt_55f
[2026-02-15T14:02:43Z] req_0abc1234 upstream 502 on next handshake: invalid-kv-offset
[2026-02-15T14:02:43Z] reconnect from 10.2.3.4: client_resume_offset=1873 server_offset=1856
```

bob_oncall: that `invalid-kv-offset` matches a bug we saw where a rotated auth session caused the runtime to create a fresh kvcache snapshot but the resume token pointed to the old snapshot -> replay/dup.

jordan_cust: oh that makes sense. Is there a client workaround until a fix lands?

carol_devex: quick mitigation: 1) increase token TTL or move rotation to occur only after stream end; 2) debounce reconnects on the client for ~5s to avoid rapid resume attempts; 3) add idempotent filtering by `last_seq` on client side (drop chunks with seq <= last_seen). We pushed a targeted fix in SDK 0.9.3 that avoids using stale resume tokens when auth refresh races with handshake.

amy_support: Jordan — we've opened INC-2026 to investigate the billing duplicate tokens. Can you confirm which region and whether you're using Redwood Hosted or Dedicated? Also please try a quick test: upgrade to python SDK 0.9.3 (we released a patch) and set `client.reconnect_debounce=5` and `client.enable_resume_validation=True` and let us know results.

jordan_cust: We're on hosted-us-east. I'll try 0.9.3 now. Quick question: how do we reproduce locally to validate before pushing to prod?

bob_oncall: easiest local repro using curl + token rotation script:
```
# open SSE with token A
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer tokenA" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?req=req_XX
# while open, rotate token to tokenB and kill client then reconnect with tokenB
```
You can also run the edge in dev-mode with `RESUME_VALIDATION=0` to see the offset drift fail earlier. For more deterministic repro, run a small loop that rapidly toggles network and rotates token every 20–40s.

carol_devex: note: PR #2345 backported the resume token atomic-swap to the 0.9.x branch. The release notes mention `fix(streaming): prevent resume token race during auth rotation` — should address the duplicate tokens & partial-frame replay.

jordan_cust: upgraded to 0.9.3 and set debounce + resume validation. After ~15m of chaos tests reconnects still happen but no duplicate fragments so far. Billing looks stable but will confirm. Thanks all.

amy_support: great, I'll keep INC-2026 open and loop billing team if we see charges. If you hit regressions, please paste `req_*` and we can pull server traces. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary deploy of runtime patch to staging started (canary-id: canary-879). Monitoring for resume token regressions.

jordan_cust: ✅ staging canary looks good; planning to roll patch to prod this evening. Appreciate the quick turnaround!
